sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: This globose cactus is endemic to Bahia in north-eastern Brazil, where it grows in dry, rocky Caatinga habitats. Its blue-green stem is about 10–40 cm tall; a reddish cephalium develops at the top of mature plants.

sections.title: Cephalium, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The ribbed stem bears spiny areoles. The cephalium is covered in wool and bristles; small magenta flowers and narrow pinkish fruits emerge from it. Ordinary stem growth does not continue above the cephalium.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: No reliable food use was found for this species; do not assume its fruits are edible.
